prompt_context_by_prefix.lpn:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): průtok
- velocity (v): rychlost
- slope (S): sklon
    DO NOT render as: activity/fitness sense of 'grade' — the treadmill or trail incline for running/walking/jogging; this is the hydraulic energy gradient, not an exercise setting; geographic or topographic landform term; school grade / academic mark
prompt_context_by_prefix.mhp:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): průtok
- penstock: tlakovod
    DO NOT render as: phonetic transliteration of the English word — translate the concept (pressure pipe / force main to turbine), never borrow 'penstock' as a loanword
- gross head (H_gross): hrubý spád
    DO NOT render as: a lazy anatomical calque that is not the local standard — an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant standard is correct; see 'head' root entry; pressure
- net head (H_net): čistý spád
    DO NOT render as: a lazy anatomical calque that is not the local standard — an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant standard is correct; see 'head' root entry; pressure
- plant efficiency (η): účinnost elektrárny
- head loss (h_L): ztráta tlakové výšky
    DO NOT render as: pressure loss / pressure drop (use the head-loss term, not the pressure term); a lazy anatomical calque that is not the local standard — an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant standard is correct; see 'head' root entry
- run-of-river: průtočná vodní elektrárna
- headworks: odběrný objekt
- junction loss (h_m): místní ztráty
- minor loss (h_m): místní ztráta

lpn.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
lpn.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

lpn.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
lpn.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

lpn.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
lpn.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

mhp.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. mhp.context: Pressure pipe carrying water from a reservoir or headpond down to a turbine in a micro-hydro system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Penstock' is a specialized term with no exact one-word equivalent in many languages. Use the established civil/hydro engineering phrase for 'pressure conduit' or 'force main to turbine'. Czech: 'tlakovod' (pressure main) is preferred over the generic 'přiváděcí potrubí' (supply pipe). Serbian: 'напорни цевовод' is the standard hydraulic engineering term. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. 2026-07-13 Task 103 follow-up: am/bn/ru values below were themselves stale phonetic transliterations of the English word (same defect class as the earlier 'riprap' audit) — corrected to compositional 'pressure pipe' phrases matching the shipped, agent-fixed lang files. When English 'penstock' itself reads as jargon, pair the primary term with a plain '(supply pipe)' gloss in the UI rather than leaving it unglossed — see mhp_diameter tooltip pattern. Task 130 (2026-07-21): the (supply pipe) gloss was applied to mhp_diameter in the 15 languages that lacked the tooltip; each language reused its existing penstock term (no term changes, wrapper+gloss only).

mhp.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

mhp.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

mhp.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. Use the energy/electrical engineering term for overall system efficiency. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

mhp.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 wave-1 sprint): ro/tr/id translations were pressure-loss-sense ('pierdere de presiune'/'basınç kaybı'/'kehilangan tekanan'), contradicting this note's own guidance. Independently flagged by both the ro and tr wave-1 translation agents; corrected to head-loss-sense ('pierdere de sarcină'/'yük kaybı'/'kehilangan tinggi tekan') to match what both agents actually used in lib/lang.ec.ro.php and lib/lang.ec.tr.php. de's 'Druckverlust' was left as-is (not flagged; German engineering practice uses pressure/head loss terms more interchangeably in pipe-flow context) but is worth a second look in a future audit. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 fa sprint): fa was 'افت فشار' (literally 'pressure loss', same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id fix above), while the fa file's own mphl_ head-loss labels already used 'افت هد' (head loss) and 'هد' is an established loanword elsewhere in the file (هد سرعت = velocity head). Standardized to 'افت هد' suite-wide for fa and fixed dw_/hw_ labels in lib/lang.ec.fa.php to match. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): glossary sw value was 'upotevu wa shinikizo' (= pressure loss), the same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id/fa fixes above. But lib/lang.ec.sw.php's own dw_main_desc/dw_main_menu/dw_main_title/mphl_main_desc/mphl_main_menu/mphl_main_title (and mpf_velocity_head, ws_headWaterHeight, or_head, mhp_gross_head elsewhere in the file) all already establish 'Kichwa' (head) as the suite's real Swahili word for hydraulic head, not 'shinikizo' (pressure). Standardized the glossary to 'upotevu wa kichwa' to match the file's own established, correct usage instead of the stale pressure-sense glossary value. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 ps wave-3 sprint): glossary ps value was 'د سر زیان' (زیان = damage/loss), but lib/lang.ec.ps.php's own dw_/hw_/mpf_/mphl_ head-loss labels (40+ occurrences suite-wide) all already use ضیاع, not زیان, for 'loss' (e.g. existing dw_main_menu 'Darcy-Weisbach د پایپ سر ضیاع', mphl_total_loss). زیان does not occur anywhere in the file. Standardized the glossary to 'د سر ضیاع' to match the file's actual established usage, same defect class as the sw fix above. Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): am confirmed on ሄድ (the ጭንቅ 'distress' mistranslation of 'head' was corrected suite-wide in this category); sw 'loss' must be Upotevu, not Hasara (financial loss) — fixed in ip_group_loss. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 ur audit found the glossary's own value (ہیڈ لاس, a transliteration) was outdated; corrected to دباؤ نقصان, the suite incumbent used 9x across dw_/hw_/mphl_ and now applied in mhp_ for consistency.

mhp.context: A hydropower configuration that uses natural river flow without a dam or significant storage reservoir. Power output varies with seasonal river flow. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: Use the established energy/hydropower sector term. 'Run' means natural river current — do not translate as jogging or running. WMO No. 385 entry 1263 gives the full facility names: Spanish 'central hidroeléctrica de pasada', French 'usine hydroélectrique au fil de l'eau', Russian 'русловая гидроэлектростанция' — these are the authoritative terms for the power plant noun. The abbreviated forms 'filo de agua' (es), 'au fil de l'eau' (fr), and 'русловая ГЭС' (ru) are standard in engineering use. German: 'Laufwasserkraftwerk'. Chinese: '径流式水电'. Task 98 audit (2026-07-13): 'micro-hydro' (the companion term this concept pairs with in mhp_ keys) had been left completely untranslated/transliterated in 4 languages, not just run-of-river — sw and km kept the raw Latin 'Micro-Hydro' embedded in otherwise-native sentences; km and ps also left 'Run-of-River' in an English parenthetical even where the surrounding sentence already translated the concept; ps separately phonetically transliterated 'مایکرو هایدرو' as its own word throughout (same defect, different script). All 4 fixed: sw → 'Umeme Mdogo wa Maji' (small electricity of water), km → 'ថាមពលវារីអគ្គិសនីខ្នាតតូច' (small-scale hydroelectric power, reusing km's own native hydro vocabulary), ps → 'کوچنی آبي ځواک' (small water-power, real Pashto not transliteration) with the redundant English '(Run-of-River)' parenthetical dropped in both km and ps since their own sentences already conveyed it. ar ('الطاقة الكهرومائية الصغيرة') and zh ('微型水力发电') were already clean and served as the quality reference for the fixes.

mhp.context: The intake structure at the upstream end of a penstock or canal, where water is diverted from the river or reservoir into the conveyance system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator (penstock diameter and length descriptions).
mhp.translation_notes: Use the civil/irrigation engineering term for a water intake or diversion structure. Spanish: 'obra de toma'. French: 'ouvrage de prise d'eau'. Russian: 'водозаборное сооружение'. German: 'Einlaufbauwerk'. In many languages, 'intake structure' is preferred over a literal translation of 'headworks'.

mhp.context: Energy loss at pipe junctions, bends, fittings, and entrance — a local (point) loss as opposed to distributed friction loss along the pipe. h_m = k_m × v²/(2g). Appears in Manning Pipe Head Loss and Micro-Hydro Power calculators.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07): the suite-wide English label for this concept is "Minor (local) loss" — 'junction loss' (formerly mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_) are merged into it; see the 'minor loss' entry for the canonical treatment. The term 'minor' is conventional but misleading — do not imply these losses are always small; the parenthetical '(local)' carries the true sense. Use the hydraulic engineering term for local/point losses at fittings. French: 'perte singulière'. Spanish: 'pérdida local' or 'pérdida por accesorio'. Russian: 'местные потери'. Chinese: '局部水头损失'. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de mphl_total_junction_k_tip aligned to örtlich/'(local)' label wording; hi/id/ur had the 'minor (local)' word order reversed against their own labels and were corrected.

mhp.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de 'Minderverlust' (=lesser/reduced loss — the exact 'smaller loss' mistranslation the item-90 convention blocks) corrected to 'Örtlicher (Einzel-)Verlust' matching the labels.

keys_to_translate.lpn_main_title: PREVIEW: Free Online Looped Pipe Network Calculator with Map Interface
keys_to_translate.lpn_main_desc: PREVIEW — Pressure and Flow in a Looped Pipe Network You Draw on a Map
keys_to_translate.lpn_preview_banner: PREVIEW — This calculator is new and still changing. It is in English only for now. See the Notes below for current limits. Comments and suggestions are always welcome.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_elev_tip: Ground or pipe level at this node. Measure it from any zero you like, as long as every node uses the same one.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_head_tip: Water surface level in the reservoir, measured as a height, not as a pressure. Leave it blank to put the water surface at the reservoir elevation.
keys_to_translate.lpn_empty_hint: To start, use the toolbar to add a background image or a reservoir, or to draw an example network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_example: This adds the example to the network you already have. Continue?
keys_to_translate.lpn_demand_tip: Flow taken out of the network at this node. Enter a negative number for flow put into the network here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_gradient_tip: Head loss divided by the length of the pipe. Use it to compare pipes of different lengths against one design limit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_head_tip: Energy of the water at this node, written as a height of water column. It is a height, not a pressure.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_clear: This permanently deletes the network, the background image, and the project name. Your settings are kept. Continue?
keys_to_translate.lpn_storage_too_new: This project was saved by a newer version of the page, so it cannot be opened here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_project_delete: Delete this project and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
keys_to_translate.lpn_storage_full: Not saved. Browser storage is full or unavailable, so your recent changes will be lost when you close this tab.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same gradient method EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_3_def: Your projects are saved automatically in this browser, and nowhere else. Clearing your browser data deletes them, and a project cannot yet be written to a file or moved to another device. Because this is an early preview, please use it for small networks and for testing only.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_4_def: Writing a project to a file, and moving one between devices, are planned. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys_to_translate.lpn_id_invalid: Enter an ID with no spaces and no quotation marks.
keys_to_translate.lpn_id_taken: That ID is already in use.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_no_fixed_head: Add a reservoir. The network needs at least one known water level before it can be solved.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_dangling_link: A pipe or pump connects to a node that no longer exists:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_unreachable: These nodes have no path to a reservoir:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_not_converged: No solution was found. Check for values that cannot be real, such as a diameter of zero.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_roughness_tip: Hazen-Williams C. A higher number means a smoother pipe: about 150 for new plastic, 130 for new steel or iron, and 100 for old pipe.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_length_tip: Length of the pipe. With Auto turned on this follows what you drew. Turn Auto off to type a length that differs from the drawing.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_km_tip: Loss from the bends, valves, and fittings on this pipe, counted as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 for a plain straight pipe.
keys_to_translate.lpn_pump_curve_ref_note: Using the curve entered for pump {id}.
keys_to_translate.lpn_pump_curve_note: One, two, or three points — see "Pump curve" in the Notes below.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_select: Mode: Select. Click an element or a label to see or change it. Drag to move a node, a vertex, or a label. Double-click a pipe to add or remove a vertex.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_delete: Mode: Delete. Click an element to remove it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_junction: Mode: Add Junction. Click the map to place a junction. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_reservoir: Mode: Add Reservoir. Click the map to place a reservoir. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_pipe: Mode: Add Pipe. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_pump: Mode: Add Pump. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_text: Mode: Add Text. Click the map to place a text label. Click near a node to attach the text to that node. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tip_select: Use this mode to change, move, and drag things on the map.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tip_labels_draggable: You can drag a label to move it. Double-click a label to put it back.
keys_to_translate.lpn_labels_decimals_tip: Decimal places shown for this label
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt1: Click two points on the background image, such as the two ends of a bar scale. Then type the real distance between them.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt2: Real distance between the two points
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt1: Click any point on the background image. This is the point you will move.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt2: Choose where that point should go, then click Continue.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_coords_prompt: Type the X,Y that point should move to
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_defaults_note: Used for elements you create from now on. Existing elements are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_push_note: Only the properties whose labels are showing right now are applied.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_confirm: Replace these properties on every existing element with the current default inputs? Values you have typed will be overwritten. You can undo this.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_none_displayed: No default input is showing as a label right now, so there is nothing to apply. Turn on the labels for the properties you want in the Labels panel, then try again.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_nothing: No existing element has any of the properties being applied.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_no_change: Every element already has these values, so nothing would change.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_tolerance_tip: How close the solver has to get before it stops. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_map_height_tip: On a small screen the map is drawn shorter than this, so that part of the page is always left to scroll.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_restore_defaults: Reset all settings (ID prefixes, default inputs, solver settings, map display, legend position, and visible labels) to their defaults? Your network is not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_wipe: Delete EVERYTHING saved for this page — every project, every background image, and all settings — and reload the page as a brand-new visitor would see it? This cannot be undone.

keys.lpn_demand_tip: Flow taken out of the network at this node. Enter a negative number for flow put into the network here.
keys.lpn_result_gradient_tip: Head loss divided by the length of the pipe. Use it to compare pipes of different lengths against one design limit.
keys.lpn_result_head_tip: Energy of the water at this node, written as a height of water column. It is a height, not a pressure.
keys.lpn_confirm_clear: This permanently deletes the network, the background image, and the project name. Your settings are kept. Continue?
keys.lpn_storage_too_new: This project was saved by a newer version of the page, so it cannot be opened here.
keys.lpn_confirm_project_delete: Delete this project and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
keys.lpn_storage_full: Not saved. Browser storage is full or unavailable, so your recent changes will be lost when you close this tab.
keys.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same gradient method EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys.lpn_notes_3_def: Your projects are saved automatically in this browser, and nowhere else. Clearing your browser data deletes them, and a project cannot yet be written to a file or moved to another device. Because this is an early preview, please use it for small networks and for testing only.
keys.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys.lpn_notes_4_def: Writing a project to a file, and moving one between devices, are planned. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys.lpn_id_invalid: Enter an ID with no spaces and no quotation marks.
keys.lpn_id_taken: That ID is already in use.
keys.lpn_diag_no_fixed_head: Add a reservoir. The network needs at least one known water level before it can be solved.
keys.lpn_diag_dangling_link: A pipe or pump connects to a node that no longer exists:
keys.lpn_diag_unreachable: These nodes have no path to a reservoir:
keys.lpn_diag_not_converged: No solution was found. Check for values that cannot be real, such as a diameter of zero.
keys.lpn_field_roughness_tip: Hazen-Williams C. A higher number means a smoother pipe: about 150 for new plastic, 130 for new steel or iron, and 100 for old pipe.
keys.lpn_field_length_tip: Length of the pipe. With Auto turned on this follows what you drew. Turn Auto off to type a length that differs from the drawing.
keys.lpn_field_km_tip: Loss from the bends, valves, and fittings on this pipe, counted as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 for a plain straight pipe.
keys.lpn_pump_curve_ref_note: Using the curve entered for pump {id}.
keys.lpn_pump_curve_note: One, two, or three points — see "Pump curve" in the Notes below.
keys.lpn_mode_select: Mode: Select. Click an element or a label to see or change it. Drag to move a node, a vertex, or a label. Double-click a pipe to add or remove a vertex.
keys.lpn_mode_delete: Mode: Delete. Click an element to remove it.
keys.lpn_mode_add_junction: Mode: Add Junction. Click the map to place a junction. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_reservoir: Mode: Add Reservoir. Click the map to place a reservoir. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_pipe: Mode: Add Pipe. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_pump: Mode: Add Pump. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_text: Mode: Add Text. Click the map to place a text label. Click near a node to attach the text to that node. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_tip_select: Use this mode to change, move, and drag things on the map.
keys.lpn_tip_labels_draggable: You can drag a label to move it. Double-click a label to put it back.
keys.lpn_labels_decimals_tip: Decimal places shown for this label
keys.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt1: Click two points on the background image, such as the two ends of a bar scale. Then type the real distance between them.
keys.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt2: Real distance between the two points
keys.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt1: Click any point on the background image. This is the point you will move.
keys.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt2: Choose where that point should go, then click Continue.
keys.lpn_backdrop_coords_prompt: Type the X,Y that point should move to
keys.lpn_settings_defaults_note: Used for elements you create from now on. Existing elements are not changed.
keys.lpn_settings_push_note: Only the properties whose labels are showing right now are applied.
keys.lpn_push_confirm: Replace these properties on every existing element with the current default inputs? Values you have typed will be overwritten. You can undo this.
keys.lpn_push_none_displayed: No default input is showing as a label right now, so there is nothing to apply. Turn on the labels for the properties you want in the Labels panel, then try again.
keys.lpn_push_nothing: No existing element has any of the properties being applied.
keys.lpn_push_no_change: Every element already has these values, so nothing would change.
keys.lpn_settings_tolerance_tip: How close the solver has to get before it stops. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer.
keys.lpn_settings_map_height_tip: On a small screen the map is drawn shorter than this, so that part of the page is always left to scroll.
keys.lpn_confirm_restore_defaults: Reset all settings (ID prefixes, default inputs, solver settings, map display, legend position, and visible labels) to their defaults? Your network is not changed.
keys.lpn_confirm_wipe: Delete EVERYTHING saved for this page — every project, every background image, and all settings — and reload the page as a brand-new visitor would see it? This cannot be undone.
